facts.raw_span: paroxysmal chest pain
The chest pain had occurred 5 times during the day, and each episode lasted 15 to 30 minutes
blood pressure and pulse rate were 106/52 mm Hg and 64 beats per minutes
normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL (normal, <0.023 ng/mL)
sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
sinus bradycardia (46 beats per minute), Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA) and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery (LMCA)

concepts.why: The patient's elevated cardiac troponin I level, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, and total occlusion of the right coronary artery support the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction.
The patient's paroxysmal chest pain, recurrent episodes of chest pain, and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery support the diagnosis of unstable angina.
The patient's total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery support the diagnosis of coronary artery occlusion.
The patient's coronary artery occlusion and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery support the diagnosis of atherosclerotic heart disease.

The patient's elevated cardiac troponin I level, ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6, and Q-wave amplitude deepening support the diagnosis of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
The patient's elevated cardiac troponin I level, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, and Q wave in lead III support the diagnosis of ST-elevation myocardial infarction.
The patient's paroxysmal chest pain, recurrent episodes of chest pain, and elevated cardiac troponin I level support the diagnosis of cardiac ischemia.
The patient's total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery support the diagnosis of coronary artery disease.
